name: Dr Priya Nair
bio: Priya has a particular interest in adult ADHD, anxiety and mood. She runs a bulk-billed clinic two days a week.

evidence.excerpt: Every ADHD review covers sleep and work, not just the script.
evidence.patientFacing: Priya reviews sleep and work stress at every ADHD appointment, not just medication.

evidence.excerpt: I did extra training in anxiety and use it daily.
evidence.patientFacing: Priya has additional training in anxiety management.

evidence.excerpt: Mood disorders are a big part of my practice.
evidence.patientFacing: Priya manages depression and low mood with regular reviews.

evidence.excerpt: I ask about sleep at every review.
evidence.patientFacing: Priya covers sleep as part of ADHD reviews.

evidence.excerpt: If we run out of time, I book another rather than rushing.
evidence.patientFacing: Priya keeps to standard appointments and books a second one when there's more to cover.
evidence.scenario: Walk me through a first appointment with a new patient.

evidence.excerpt: I send a written summary with the reasons after each visit.
evidence.patientFacing: Priya sends a written summary of the plan and the reasons for it after each visit.
evidence.scenario: A patient asks why you're recommending a particular plan.

evidence.excerpt: Mood and anxiety are always on the agenda with ADHD.
evidence.patientFacing: Priya looks at mood, anxiety and ADHD together at every review.
evidence.scenario: A patient comes in about ADHD medication but mentions poor sleep and stress.

evidence.excerpt: I see people every four to six weeks while we're adjusting.
evidence.patientFacing: Priya books regular reviews every few weeks while things are changing.
evidence.scenario: What happens between appointments for your ongoing patients?

evidence.excerpt: I go through the options and we agree together.
evidence.patientFacing: Priya goes through the options with you and agrees on a plan together.
evidence.scenario: A patient strongly prefers a treatment you do not initially recommend.

evidence.excerpt: I give the context first, then the recommendation.
evidence.patientFacing: Priya explains results with context before recommendations.
evidence.scenario: You need to tell a patient a test result isn't what they hoped.

evidence.excerpt: Medication is one tool among several.
evidence.patientFacing: Priya considers medication alongside other options.
evidence.scenario: A patient asks whether they should start medication.
